title: 2. Build from the Same Core: Parallel Character Construction
use_cases: Use when you want to establish thematic resonance between the protagonist and antagonist
Implement when writing stories centered around the themes of choice and consequence
Configure when developing a 'mirror' villain to highlight the protagonist's moral arc
Use when comparing how different reactions to shared trauma define a character's alignment
content:
Your antagonist should feel like they came from the same origin but made a different choice. Same background. Same trauma. Different conclusion.

Harry Potter and Voldemort. Both orphans. Both gifted. Voldemort chooses domination. Harry chooses love and connection.

Killmonger and T’Challa. Black Widow and Yelena. The parallels matter because they force the audience to ask: What would I choose?

Use this technique when: You want thematic resonance, or when you’re writing a story about choice, fate, or morality.
